Build a Covariate Design Matrix With a Config-Chosen Fixed-Effect Stratifier

Source: R/profile_joint_bernoulli.R
profile_build_fixed_effect_design.Rd

Builds the X matrix profile_build_design expects, for the ONE joint model this family fits across every configured stratum at once – never a silent separate fit per stratum. The interaction coefficients profile_build_design builds (eta) have no stratum index at all (they are defined purely over the state space), so they are automatically SHARED across every level of whatever stratifier this function encodes here; nothing downstream needs to know what that stratifier was.

Usage

profile_build_fixed_effect_design(
  ids,
  group_col = "group",
  covariates = NULL,
  contrast = c("reference", "sum_to_zero"),
  reference_level = NULL
)

Arguments

ids

Data frame, one row per event, matching profile_prepare_model_data's $ids row order (its own $ids is the intended input, but any data frame with a stratum column works).

group_col

Character or NULL. Column in ids naming the fixed-effect stratifier – hospital, state, district, country, whatever the config specifies. Default "group", matching profile_prepare_model_data()$ids's own column name. NULL means NO fixed effects (fully pooled) – an explicit, valid choice, not something to avoid by default.

covariates

Data frame or NULL, same row order as ids (profile_prepare_model_data()$covariates is the intended input). Additional covariates (age, sex, ...) included alongside the stratifier. Default NULL (stratifier + intercept only).

contrast

Character, "reference" (default) or "sum_to_zero". "reference" drops one level (reference_level) and keeps an intercept – standard treatment coding. "sum_to_zero" uses deviation-from-grand-mean coding instead, with no dropped reference level.

reference_level

Character or NULL. Which level of group_col is dropped, when contrast = "reference". NULL (default) uses the first level alphabetically – R's own default, made explicit and recorded here rather than left implicit.

Value

A list: X (the design matrix), term_names (colnames(X), in order), group_col (echoed, NULL if no stratifier), reference_level (the dropped level, NA for sum_to_zero or no stratifier), contrast (echoed), levels (every level of group_col present, in the order used), rank (qr(X)$rank – always == ncol(X), or the function has already stopped).

Details

The stratifier itself is never assumed to be "hospital": it is whatever column the caller's analysis config names via group_col – hospital, state, district, country, or NULL for no fixed effects at all (a fully pooled single-intercept model). That choice belongs to whoever prepares the config in anumaan-analysis, exactly like group_col is already generic everywhere else in this family (profile_audit_support, profile_prepare_model_data, ...) – this function does not special-case hospitals, and does not decide the granularity for the caller.

Guards against the failure mode an unconstrained design invites: a full set of stratum dummy columns PLUS an intercept is rank-deficient (aliased) – contrast = "reference" drops one declared/default level instead, and contrast = "sum_to_zero" uses deviation-from- grand-mean coding with no dropped reference level at all. Either way, the returned design's rank is checked and a rank deficiency (from this or from collinear covariates) stops with a specific diagnosis rather than silently fitting an unidentified model.
